description: Agreement between hand labels (experiments/e01/labels.json) and the LLM auto-grader (src/grade.py, model anthropic/claude-opus-4.8 via OpenRouter) on the same 29 non-truncated pilot responses, before and after the GRADER.md spec revision (rung 0 exclusivity language, 2a pronoun requirement, 3 attributee requirement).

grader_v2.grader_md_version: post-revision (current GRADER.md at time of this run)

hypothesis_not_finding: The spec revision (rung 0 exclusivity wording, stricter 2a/3 definitions) appears to improve highest_rung agreement with hand labels from 75.9% to 82.8% on this n=29 sample. NOT a confirmed finding.
two_likely_artifacts: n=29 is small; a 2-record swing (22->24 matches) is within noise for a binomial at this sample size. No significance test has been run.

The rung-0 exclusivity violation rate dropped from 5/29 to 3/29 without any change to src/grade.py's system prompt -- the improvement could be incidental spec wording changes (e.g. the 3/6 attributee clarification reducing spurious rung-0+3 co-assignments) rather than the exclusivity rule itself landing better. The exclusivity bug is not fixed, only less frequent; grade.py's system prompt still just embeds GRADER.md verbatim and does not re-emphasize the exclusivity constraint.
remaining_open_issue: Rung 4 vs 5 accounts for most remaining highest_rung mismatches (indices 8, 10, 13, 26 involve a 4/5 or 3/5 split) -- expected, since the grader cannot browse URLs and GRADER.md instructs it to default to rung 5 + needs_url_check when it can't verify, while hand labels presumably resolved the URL.
